verdicts.reason: Both break the product art the same way: the cream circle has come off the bottle and sits clipped at the bottom-left, and the bottle has lost its fill, leaving a thin outline with its sun and leaf decorations floating. The text and CTA are fine but small, with lots of empty orange around them. A keeps 'Out now.' a bit closer to the headline. B's bottle is slightly more solid but the subtitle is further from the headline, so the text group is looser. The difference is very small.

A has the broken product art described above (circle detached and clipped, bottle hollow), but its headline and 'Try It' button are still readable and in the right places. B has the same broken art, and on top of that the CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill dropped at the bottom edge. Its label is unreadable, so the hierarchy fails and the action is effectively gone.

A drops the bottle entirely, so the main product image is lost. 'Out now.' sits on top of the leftover cream circle, the headline is pushed against the left edge, and a stray tiny artifact appears near the bottom. That leaves the ad without its product and makes it unusable. B is the shared candidate with the broken product art (detached, clipped circle and hollow bottle), but its headline, subtitle and CTA are in order and readable.
